snippets.text: The second essential feature of stroke is its focal signature. The neurologic deficit reflects both the location and the size of the infarct or hemorrhage. Hemiplegia stands as the most typical sign of stroke, whether in the cerebral hemisphere or brainstem, but there are many other manifestations, occurring in recognizable combinations. These include paralysis, numbness, and sensory deficits of many types on one side of the body, aphasia, visual field defects, diplopia, dizziness, dysarthria, and so forth. The neurovascular syndromes enable the physician to localize the lesion—sometimes so precisely that even the affected arterial branch can be specified—and to indicate whether the lesion is an infarct or a hemorrhage. These syndromes are described in the sections that follow. This group of diseases has also provided the most instructive approach to localization in neurology. As our colleague C.M. A.rationale: Apical lung tumor is another term for Pancoast tumor, which is a type of lung cancer that affects the upper part of the lung and can cause neurological symptoms.

B.rationale: Brachial plexopathy refers to damage or injury to the brachial plexus, which is a network of nerves that originates in the spinal cord and controls muscle movements in the arm and hand.

D.rationale: Scalenus anticus syndrome, also known as thoracic outlet syndrome, is a condition that occurs when the nerves or blood vessels in the thoracic outlet, which is the space between the neck and shoulder, are compressed.

E.rationale: Subclavian steal syndrome is a condition that occurs when the subclavian artery, which supplies blood to the arm, is compressed or blocked, causing blood to be diverted from the brain to the arm.
